summary.intent: Run an adversarial design review on a memory-loop spec (covering keyword matching, memory editing, and generation thresholds), then iteratively update the spec to address all findings until it is ready for implementation planning.
summary.outcome: Two rounds of adversarial review were completed; the spec was updated after each pass to address blocking issues including keyword phrase matching semantics, singleton policy tri-state, override validation, editor failure modes, edit history with previous values, concurrency/persistence safety, and settings UI indicators.

repo: Keywords in the memory-loop system are exact phrase matches (case-insensitive strings.Contains), not tokenized — 'go test' matches the literal substring, not 'go' OR 'test' independently.
Singleton policy was changed from a bool to a tri-state string: 'all', 'review-rules', 'none'.
FingerprintForRecord is computed from (kind, title, body) only — keywords do not affect the fingerprint.
Fingerprints are used only for reconciliation, not as stable IDs elsewhere.
RefreshHistory should store ThresholdOverride flag and full ResolvedConfig, not just the preset name.
Override validation: numeric values are clamped to valid ranges; invalid string values fall back to preset with a warning.
$EDITOR values like 'code --wait' must be parsed with strings.Fields() before exec.Command.
Edit history events must capture prev_title, prev_body, prev_keywords for recoverability.
Keyword parsing rules: trim whitespace, remove empty entries, deduplicate, max 10, min 2 chars.
The balanced preset must exactly match current hardcoded values to avoid silent behavior changes on upgrade.
Strict mode with 3 evidence sessions should show a hint in TUI/CLI for new repos with insufficient history.

code.finding: Spec was iteratively updated across two adversarial review cycles; final version covers phrase matching, tri-state singleton policy, override validation, editor failure modes, edit history with prev values, concurrency, persistence failure, clear-overrides CLI flag, and settings UI override indicator.

workflow: The Codex companion script hits ENOBUFS buffer overflow when the working tree contains large binary/db files (e.g. insights.db) — running it as a subagent directly on the target file is a reliable workaround.
Adversarial review should be framed as a challenge of design choices and assumptions, not just an implementation defect pass.
Iterating spec → adversarial review → update spec is an effective loop for hardening designs before implementation planning.
When a user confirms a design intent mid-session (e.g. 'keywords are phrases'), update the spec immediately to make the clarification canonical.

friction: Codex companion script failed with ENOBUFS due to large untracked binary files (insights.db) in the working tree when attempting to scope the review.
The --wait flag workaround also failed; had to fall back to running the adversarial review as a Claude subagent directly on the spec file.
The spec had a duplicate '### Reconciliation' header that needed cleanup.
open_items: Implementation plan for the memory-loop edit/keywords/threshold feature has not yet been written — spec is ready but plan step was deferred pending user review.
The modified files listed (queries.go, summary_cmd.go, etc.) suggest related CLI work may be in progress in the agent-improvements worktree but were not discussed in this session.
No discussion of how keywords interact with memory scoping (cross-cutting concern noted but may need further elaboration in implementation).
Performance impact of phrase matching at scale (noted as acceptable but not benchmarked).
